text:
deploy-bot: config-only deploy queued for svc-inference (config id: cfg-20260318-12). Changes: request_limits, per_request_timeout_ms, routing_policy, batching_params. Rolling out to prod with canary=5% for 10m. Link to diff: https://redwood.internal/changes/cfg-20260318-12

alice: saw the diff, main change is pref max_pending_requests -> 200 (was 500). Why reduce?

ben: reducing pending_requests to avoid queuing on spike, will drop requests earlier. intended to force upstream backpressure. See comment in PR.

carol: worried about latency regressions if we lower max_batch_size from 64->32. Any perf numbers?

jamie: perf lab run attached. p99 increased from 220ms->260ms at steady state, but tail improves under burst. tradeoff seems OK. https://ci/reports/123

sre-oncall: @jamie can you hold channel if we see errors? what's rollback plan?

jamie: yes, rollback policy: config-only change, we can revert to cfg-20260316 within 1 click; deploy-bot supports immediate rollback. Also can pin traffic routing to "low-cost" vs "low-latency" buckets.

alice: can we pin the model_version for the canary? want to avoid mixing model rollouts with config-only.

jamie: pinned model sha: model-1.2.3, added in config.

devops-bot: deploy started at 1712001234, canary=5%, window=10m

alice: monitoring: dashboards in ops -> svc-inference -> latency, errors. I'll watch keys: 429s, 504s, p95.

ben: note: timeouts changed from 30000ms -> 15000ms. That could surface as 504s if upstream slow.

carol: update release notes (short): 'Config-only: lower request queue limit, shorter per-request timeout, routing favors lower-cost variants, reduce max_batch_size to limit tail latency'.

jamie: added release note at https://docs/releases/2026-03-18

sre-oncall: 2m into canary: no spikes in 5xx. p95 stable. continuing.

deploy-bot: canary check passed at +10m, progressing to 50%

alice: holding for 30m at 50% before full.

devops-bot: progressed to 50% at 1712001834

sre-oncall: at 50% p99 is 280ms, 5xx still low. good.

ben: I'm going to adjust routing policy to set fallback_model_variant to 'small' in case of overload.

jamie: pushed small fallback var in config. snippet:
```
routing:
  policy: cost_preference
  fallback_variant: small
```

alice: agree. we should document in release notes that 'fallback variant added'.

carol: question: does this affect Dedicated customers? They have pinning. We should ensure not rolled there.

jamie: this rollout targets hosted only; Dedicated customers are excluded by default in rollout config.

sre-oncall: 30m at 50% done, proceeding to 100%.

deploy-bot: rollout complete at 1712003034. If rollback needed run: /deploy rollback cfg-20260316

alice: updating customer-facing release note in #announcements after security review.

ben: closing thread. :checkered_flag:
